**Voica v0.8.1 — a stray capital letter after a filler, and terms recognised from a little further away.**

### Fixed: a capital in the middle of a sentence

Removing a filler sometimes handed a capital letter to the word that took its place, in the middle
of a sentence: "их закрыли, Хмм, потом решили" came out as "их закрыли, **П**отом решили".

The reason is that recognition writes a filler capitalized as if it were a remark of its own, so its
capital says nothing about where a sentence begins. Now only the punctuation left behind decides —
except at the very start of the text, where there is none. What the rule was built for still works:
"…на улицу. э-э, на работу" still becomes "…на улицу. На работу".

If you dictate with the filler clean-up on (it is on by default), this one was reaching your text.

### Changed: terms are pulled back from a little further

A garbled term now needs to be 50% similar to the vocabulary entry rather than 60%, matching the
cross-platform spec. This came from a measurement rather than a guess: over a 138-line history the
replacements were identical at either value, and the only thing the change adds here is a live case
— the engine wrote `Depsic`, which lands exactly on the old bar and was left alone.

Nothing became less careful. What keeps "Greek" from turning into "Groq" was never this number: the
two differ by their consonant skeletons.

Also: the recognition-engine hint in Settings now says what has been true since 0.8.0 — the
vocabulary hint during recognition is cloud-only, but the term rules work on both engines, and the
local engine is where they help most.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.8.1.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
